task_outline:
- Build a shared monthly time-spine used by every new schedule: a header block naming the individual (pulled from the Input tab name cell) and the schedule title, plus a three-row column header, followed by 1,001 monthly rows. Column A is the integer month counter beginning at 0 and stepping by 1 through 1000; column B is the end-of-month date built by EOMONTH of the model start date offset by the month counter; column C is the person's age at that date via DATEDIF from their birthday. This spine is replicated identically across all 14 new tabs, with Person A tabs referencing Individual #1's inputs and Person B tabs referencing Individual #2's inputs.
- Add Salary_01 and Salary_02 (Salary & Health Insurance) schedules with columns for Gross Salary, Social Security tax, Medicare tax, Health Insurance, 401(k) employee contribution, Federal Taxes, State Taxes, and Net Pay. Row 4 (month 0) uses the raw starting monthly salary hardcoded to the input; from row 5 onward, gross salary grows at the annual raise rate compounded by whole-year DATEDIF from model start, zeroed once past the person's retirement date. Social Security and Medicare are negative percentages of gross using the global payroll-tax rates. Health insurance is the base pre-tax premium escalated by the health-cost inflation rate compounded by years elapsed, zeroed after death. The 401(k) employee contribution is the lesser (in magnitude) of gross × employee-contribution % and the annual IRS max ÷ 12, zeroed after retirement. Federal and State taxes are the applicable rates applied to (gross + health insurance + 401(k)), zeroed after retirement. Net Pay sums all columns and zeroes after death.
- Add 401k_01 and 401k_02 schedules with columns for Employer Contribution, Employee Contribution, Retirement Distribution, and running Balance, plus a one-cell "Balance At Retirement" lookup. Row 4 seeds the balance with the current 401(k) input and hardcodes the three flow columns to 0. From row 5 onward, employer contribution = Salary tab gross × employer-match %, employee contribution = −1 × the Salary tab's 401(k) cell, and the running balance = prior balance plus the three flows, all grown by monthly return (annual return ÷ 1200), zeroed after death. The distribution is a PMT computed only between the payout-start date and the death date, using the monthly return rate, term = number of months from payout start to death (via OFFSET/MATCH on the date column), present value = the balance-at-retirement lookup, and future value = −1 × the target remaining balance at death. The "Balance At Retirement" cell in row 4 uses OFFSET/MATCH to pull the balance from the row whose date matches the payout-start date.
- Add IRA_01 and IRA_02 (Traditional IRA) schedules with columns for Monthly Contribution, Retirement Distribution, and Balance, plus a "Balance At Retirement" lookup cell. Row 4 seeds the balance from the current Traditional IRA input and hardcodes contribution and distribution to 0. From row 5, the monthly contribution equals the input's monthly IRA contribution while both individuals are pre-retirement (else 0). The distribution mirrors the 401(k) PMT construction — active only between payout-start and death, using IRA rate/(100×12), term measured by OFFSET/MATCH on the date column, PV = the balance-at-retirement lookup, FV = 0. Balance rolls forward as (prior + contribution + distribution) × (1 + monthly return).
- Add Roth_01 and Roth_02 schedules with the same three-column structure (Monthly Contribution, Distribution, Balance) plus a "Balance At Retirement" cell keyed off the retirement date (not the 59½ payout date). Contributions apply while both individuals are pre-retirement; distributions are PMT-driven between retirement and death using the Roth rate; the balance rolls forward with monthly compounding at the Roth rate of return.
- Add Invest_01 and Invest_02 (taxable Investment Account) schedules mirroring the Roth pattern: contribution equals the input's monthly invest-account contribution while both individuals are pre-retirement; distribution is a PMT from retirement to death using the investment-account rate and the balance-at-retirement lookup; balance rolls forward with monthly compounding at the investment-account rate of return.
- Add SocialSec_01 and SocialSec_02 schedules containing only a single Payout column. Each row returns the input's Social Security monthly payout when the current date falls between the Social Security payout-start date and the death date, otherwise 0.
- Add Pension_01 and Pension_02 schedules containing only a single Payout column, structured identically to Social Security but keyed off the pension payout-start date and pension payout amount from the input.
- Add Retirement_Dist_01 and Retirement_Dist_02 consolidating tabs with columns for Tax-Deferred Distributions, Tax-Free Distributions, Federal Taxes, State Taxes, and Net Distribution. Tax-deferred distributions = −(401(k) distribution + IRA distribution + Investment distribution) + Pension payout + Social Security payout, all pulled from the matching-suffix schedules for that individual. Tax-free distributions = −Roth distribution. Federal and State taxes are the tax-deferred total multiplied by the negative of the federal and state rates. Net Distribution sums the tax-deferred, tax-free, federal, and state columns to produce the final after-tax retirement cash flow per person per month.
transition_description: Delete tabs: Salary_01, Salary_02, 401k_01, 401k_02, IRA_01, IRA_02, Roth_01, Roth_02, Invest_01, Invest_02, SocialSec_01, SocialSec_02, Pension_01, Pension_02, Retirement_Dist_01, Retirement_Dist_02

task_outline:

- Create the new Fair Market Value Analysis tab with a Valuation Assumptions header block containing WACC of 20%, Terminal Growth Rate of 0%, Effective Tax Rate of 40%, Expense Inflation of 0%, Capital Expenditures of 150000, Beginning Fixed Assets pulled from the balance sheet's fixed assets line, Average Depreciation Life of 7, Interest Bearing Debt of 0, Bad Debt as % of NPR of 1.5%, Minority/Marketability Discount of 0%, Incremental Working Capital Requirement of 20%, Shares/Units in Partnership of 100, and Excess Cash of 0; lay out a time axis with a Base Year column plus Year 1 through Year 5 projection columns and a Terminal Year column.
- Build the volume-and-price revenue driver block: Annual Cases seeded from Backup Cases and grown by an Annual Case Growth driver (0% in every year); Net Revenue Per Case computed in the base year as Net Revenue ÷ Cases and grown by an Annual Net Revenue/Case Growth driver (0% in every year); Net Revenue in the base year pulled from Backup and in projection years computed as Cases × Revenue per Case, with the Terminal Year Net Revenue grown by the terminal growth rate; add a Net Revenue Growth check row.
- Build the Operating Expenses block with a base-year split of Salary Related into two halves — one grown with volume-and-inflation and one grown with inflation only — plus Medical Supplies (volume × inflation), Variable Expenses (inflation), Bad Debt (% of Net Revenue via the 1.5% assumption), Management Fee grown at 2.5% annually (with a hardcode of 1.025), and Fixed Costs (inflation); sum to a Total Operating Expense line.
- Build a supporting Cost-per-Case sub-schedule under the expense block deriving base-year unit costs for each expense category (each expense ÷ base-year cases), then rolling per-case costs forward: the volume-and-inflation lines (Salary volume half, Medical Supplies) grow by expense inflation and are multiplied back by projected cases to drive their expense rows, while the inflation-only, %-of-revenue, and management-fee lines derive their per-case values from the calculated total expense divided by projected cases.
- Compute EBITDA as Net Revenue less Total Operating Expense with an EBITDA Margin check; pull Depreciation & Amortization from the Depreciation Schedule for the projection and terminal years, with the base year computed as Beginning Fixed Assets ÷ 7-year life; derive EBIT, apply Corporate & State Taxes at the 40% rate, and arrive at Net Income.
- Build a Cash Flow Analysis block below Net Income: start from Net Income, add back Depreciation & Amortization, deduct incremental working capital (change in Net Revenue × 20% requirement), and deduct Capital Expenditure (Year 1 seeded from the 150000 assumption, grown by inflation through Year 5, with Terminal capex set equal to terminal D&A to maintain steady-state); sum to Debt Free Net Discretionary Cash Flow.
- Build the DCF valuation stack: Terminal Value equal to Terminal Year cash flow ÷ (WACC − terminal growth); a Period row starting at 0.5 in Year 1 and incrementing by 1 through Year 5, with Terminal set at 5; a Discount Factor row of 1/(1+WACC)^Period; a Present Value (Years 1–5) row summed across the projection columns; a Present Value Terminal row; and Fair Market Value (Total Capital) as the sum of the two, with each PV component shown as a % of total.
- Build the equity bridge below the FMV: subtract Interest Bearing Debt (using the 0 assumption), add Excess Cash, arrive at Fair Market Value Equity (Enterprise/Control Level), apply the Minority/Marketability Discount to get Fair Market Value Equity (Minority Level), and divide by the 100 units of ownership to yield Fair Market Value per Unit of Ownership.
- Build a Market Multiples sanity-check block to the right of the equity bridge showing TMC/Revenue, TMC/EBITDA, and TMC/EBIT (each as Total FMV ÷ the corresponding Base Year, Year 1, Year 2, and Year 3 line from the projection).

Reuse the same stub / half-year discount period logic, compute a PV Factor at the 10% cost of capital, discount each period's Invested Capital to PV, and sum to Net Present Value of Invested Capital.

- In the Retailer tab, add the cost and working-capital columns: OVERHEAD EXPENSES = UNITS SOLD × Retailer overhead; HOLDING COST = ENDING INVENTORY × Retailer holding cost per unit; SHORTAGE COST = LOST SALES × Retailer shortage cost per unit; INVENTORY WEEKS = ROUNDUP(ENDING INVENTORY ÷ average demand, 0); CASH TO CASH CYCLE TIME = INVENTORY WEEKS + Customer→Retailer credit − Retailer→Distributor credit; ACCOUNTS PAYABLE = PURCHASE COST offset back 2 periods + OVERHEAD; ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE = INVOICE TO CUSTOMER.
